Rashi on Niddah 24a:11:1.english: As a stringency - That you deemed her impure for two weeks due to the uncertainty of [it being] a female.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:11:2.hebrew: חומרא דאתי לידי קולא הוא - דכיון דולד הוא, יהביתו לה ימי טוהר, מיהא ל"ג דזכר, ומטהריתו לדם ראייתה שלא כדין, דטמאה נדה היא, דלאו ולד הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:11:2.english: It is a stringency that leads to a leniency - For since [you hold that] it is an offspring, you give her days of purity, at least the thirty-three [days] of a male, and you deem the blood of her sightings pure unlawfully, for she is impure as a niddah, since it is not an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:12:1.hebrew: בבהמה אסור באכילה - אם נשחטה אמו ונמצא במעיה, וכל שכן יצא לאויר העולם, דנפל הוא ונבלה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:12:1.english: In [the case of] an animal, it is forbidden to be eaten - [Even] if its mother was slaughtered and it was found in her womb, and all the more so if it emerged into the airspace of the world, for it is a non-viable birth and a carcass.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:12:2.hebrew: מותר באכילה - דכתיב (ויקרא י״א:ג׳) כל בבהמה תאכלו, כל הנמצא בבהמה תאכלו, ובלבד שיהיו לו פרסות או פרסה, כדאמר בבהמה המקשה לילד (חולין סט:):
Rashi on Niddah 24a:12:2.english: Permitted for consumption - For it is written (Leviticus 11:3): "Whatever is in an animal you may eat" — [meaning] whatever is found inside an animal you may eat, provided that it has hooves or a hoof, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] "Behemah HaMaksheh Leiled" (Chullin 69b).

Rashi on Niddah 24a:13:1.hebrew: השסועה - רחמנא אסרה, דכתיב (דברים יד) את זה לא תאכלו וגו' השסועה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:13:1.english: The cleft creature - The Merciful One prohibited it, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14): "These you shall not eat... the cleft creature."

Rashi on Niddah 24a:14:1.hebrew: רב סבר - האי דאסר רחמנא, כשנמצאת במעי בהמה אסורה, דהא בריה בעלמא בפני עצמה ליתא:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:14:1.english: Rav holds - That which the Merciful One forbade [is that] when it is found in the womb of an animal, it is forbidden, for there is no [such] creature in the world on its own.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:14:2.hebrew: בעלמא אגמריה - אותו המין אסר, אבל אם נמצאת במעי פרה מותר:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:14:2.english: He taught it to him in the world - [The Merciful One] forbade that species, but if it is found in the womb of a cow, it is permitted.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:15:1.hebrew: ר' חנינא בן אנטיגנוס - בבכור קאי, וקאמר דהוי מום, ומדפסל ליה לקרבן — מכלל דלהדיוט שרי. וקשיא לתרוייהו: דהא אפי' יצא לאויר העולם שרי, ושמואל לא שרי אלא במעי אמו. והא דאקשי רב שימי טפי לרב מדשמואל — משום דגביה הוה קאי, ובר בריה הוה, כדאמר בפרק כל הבשר (חולין קיא:): רב אקלע לבי רב שימי בר חייא בר בריה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:15:1.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus - He is referring to a firstborn [animal], and states that this is a blemish; and since he disqualifies it as an offering, it follows by implication that for an ordinary person it is permitted. And this poses a difficulty to both of them, for behold, even [if it] emerged into the airspace of the world it is permitted, whereas Shmuel permitted [it] only in its mother's womb. And as for the fact that Rav Shimi raised the objection against Rav rather than against Shmuel, [it is] because he was standing before him and was his grandson, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter "Kol HaBasar" (Chullin 111b): "Rav visited the home of Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya, his grandson."

Rashi on Niddah 24a:15:2.hebrew: שימי את - בכמה דוכתין אשכחן דמהדר ליה רב הכי: שימי את. ונראה בעיני משום דבר בריה הוה, וקאמר ליה הכי משום חביבותיה, כלומר: אתה יודע להשיבני. ואני שמעתי, שמדת צניעות היה בו ברב, שלא היה זוקף עיניו למעלה, הלכך לא היה מכירו. ולא נהירא לי, שהרי לא מצינו שאמר רב כך לשום אדם, אלא לזה אמר כן בכמה מקומות: כאן ובמנחות (דף קי.). ועוד שמעתי, משום דחריף הוה ודחיק ליה, כי ההיא דאמר (במועד קטן (דף כט)): רחמנא לישזבא מכיסופיה דרב שימי. ולא היא, דהתם רב שימי בר אשי הוה דדחיק ליה לרב פפא:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:15:2.english: Are you Shimi? - In several places we find that Rav responded to him thus: "Are you Shimi?" And it appears to me [that it was] because he was his grandson, and he said this to him out of affection, meaning: You know [how] to challenge me! And I heard that Rav possessed a trait of modesty, in that he would not raise his eyes upward; therefore, he did not recognize him. But this does not seem correct to me, for we do not find that Rav said so to any [other] person, but rather he said so only to this one in several places: here and in Menachot (page 110a). And furthermore I heard [that it was] because he was sharp and pressed him [with difficulties], like that which is said (in Moed Katan (page 29)): "May the Merciful One save [us] from the humiliation of Rav Shimi!" But it is not so, for there it was Rav Shimi bar Ashi who pressed Rav Pappa.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:15:3.hebrew: ששדרתו עקומה - הא דרבי חנינא דמשמע דחיי, לאו שני גבין ממש, אלא ששדרתו עקומה (כזה) ונראין כשתים:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:15:3.english: Whose spine is crooked - This [teaching] of Rabbi Ḥanina, which implies that it survives, is not [referring to] two actual backs, but rather that its spine is crooked (like this) and they appear as two.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:16:1.hebrew: יש בעוברין - שיצאו לאויר העולם, שאסורין משום נבלה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:16:1.english: There are among fetuses - [Those] that emerged into the airspace of the world, which are forbidden as a carcass.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:17:1.hebrew: לאו יצא מכלל עוברין - דהני, אע"ג דלא כלו חדשיהן, כי נמצאו במעי אמן שרו, אבל האי, אפי' במעי אמן אסור, וקשיא לשמואל:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:17:1.english: Does it not mean excluded from the category of fetuses - For these [other fetuses], even though their months [of gestation] were not completed, when they are found in their mother's womb they are permitted, but this one, even in its mother's womb is forbidden; and this poses a difficulty for Shmuel.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:18:1.hebrew: רב מתרץ לטעמיה - דרב לא צריך לתרוצי אלא משום היא גופה, דלא משתמע שפיר; דהא רישא כשיצאו לאויר העולם מיירי, וסיפא דקתני יצא משמע דעלה קאי, וכשיצא לאויר העולם משמע דמותר, ואי אפשר לומר כן. הלכך צריך להוסיף עליה: אבל במעי אמו שרי, דכתיב כל בבהמה תאכלו, בפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין סט.):
Rashi on Niddah 24a:18:1.english: Rav resolves according to his reasoning - For Rav did not need to resolve [it] except because of [the baraita] itself, which is not clearly understood; for the opening clause deals with when they emerged into the airspace of the world, and the latter clause, which teaches "[if it] emerged," implies that it refers to it, and that when it emerged into the airspace of the world, it implies that it is permitted, and it is impossible to say so. Therefore, one must add to it: "But in its mother's womb it is permitted," as it is written: "all [that is] in the beast you may eat," in the chapter "Behemah HaMaksheh" (Chullin 69a).

Rashi on Niddah 24a:19:1.hebrew: יצא מי שיש לו שני גבין וכו' - דכי כתב רחמנא השסועה למיסר, במעי אמו אסרה, דהא מין בפני עצמה ליתא:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:19:1.english: This excludes one that has two backs, etc. - For when the Merciful One wrote of the shesuah to forbid [it], He forbade it in its mother's womb, since it does not exist as an independent species.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:1:1.hebrew: עד הארכובה - שנחתכו רגליה עד למעלה מן הארכובה, שהיא טרפה, וקסבר: טרפה אינה חיה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:1:1.english: Until the knee - That its legs were severed up to above the knee, for it is a tereifa, and he holds that a tereifa cannot survive.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:1:2.hebrew: עד לנקביו - ונקביו בכלל. קסבר: טרפה חיה, הלכך עד לארכובה הוי ולד, אבל עד לנקביו הוי נבלה, כר' אלעזר דאמר: ניטל הירך וחלל שלה נבלה, ואפי' בחייה מטמאה, הלכך לא חיה. ובשחיטת חולין (דף כא.) מפרש היכי דמי חלל שלה: כל שרבוצה ונראית חסרה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:1:2.english: Until his orifices - And his orifices are included. [Rabbi Yannai] holds that a *tereifa* can survive; therefore, [if severed only] up to the knee, it is [considered] an offspring. But [if severed] up to his orifices, it is [considered] a carcass, in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, who said: "[If] the thigh and its cavity were removed, [it is] a carcass," and even during its lifetime it imparts ritual impurity; therefore, it cannot survive. And in [tractate] Sheḥitat Chullin (page 21a), [the Gemara] explains what constitutes "its cavity": Any [animal] that, when lying down, appears lacking.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:1:3.hebrew: עד טבורו - אבל עד נקביו לא, דלית ליה דרבי אלעזר. ואי משום טרפה — קסבר טרפה חיה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:1:3.english: Until his navel - But [if removed only] until his orifices, [it would] not [die], for he does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Elazar; and if [one might say that it dies] because it is a tereifa, he holds that a tereifa can survive.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:3:1.english: Between Rabbi Yannai and Rabbi Yoḥanan, the difference between them is [the ruling] of Rabbi Elazar - And both of them hold that a tereifah can survive.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:4:1.english: From above - That [a piece] was cut from its skull.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:5:1.hebrew: כמין אפקתא דדיקלא - שהדקל למטה יחיד ומתפצל מלמעלה, כך היו ידיו ורגליו על כתפו, ומלמטה הוא בלא צורה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:5:1.english: Like the branching of a palm tree - For [just as] a palm tree is single below and branches out above, so were its hands and feet on its shoulder, and below it was without form.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:6:1.hebrew: מוסמסין - מעוכין קצת, ולא כל כך כפניו טוחות:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:6:1.english: Mashed - Somewhat crushed, and not as much as [in the case where] its face is flattened.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:8:1.english: When they disagree, [it is] where its face is smoothed over - That no form is discernible in it at all.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:8:2.hebrew: ואיפכא איתמר - ולא משום צורך מפיק לה, אלא הכי גמר לה מרביה:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:8:2.english: And the opposite was stated - And not out of necessity does he state it, but rather this is how he learned it from his teacher.

Rashi on Niddah 24a:9:1.hebrew: לותביה ריש לקיש לר' יוחנן מהא - דאם איתא, ליתני: או ממי שפניו טוחות:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:9:1.english: Let Reish Lakish object to Rabbi Yoḥanan from this - For if it is so, let [the baraita] teach: "Or from one whose face is flat."

Rashi on Niddah 24a:9:2.hebrew: היינו פניו טוחות - אבל בפניו מוסמסין ליכא לשנויי הכי, דהא ניכרת בהן הצורה, ולאו אטום הוא, דאטום היינו חסר לגמרי:
Rashi on Niddah 24a:9:2.english: That is [one whose] face is flat - But regarding [a fetus whose] face is mashed, one cannot answer like this, for the form is discernible in them, and it is not "sealed," for "sealed" means missing entirely.

Tosafot on Niddah 24a:15:1.hebrew: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס אומר כל שיש כו' - פ"ה: מדהוי מום לקרבן, מכלל דלהדיוט שרי. וקשה לתרוייהו, דהא אפי' יצא לאויר העולם שרי, ושמואל לא שרי ליה אלא במעי אמו. וקשה לר"ת, דבפ' אלו מומין (דף מג:) תנא ליה גבי מומי כהן, ולא גבי מומי בהמה; והתם נמי פריך מרב, ולא מייתי משמואל מידי. ונראה לר"ת, דארב דוקא פריך, דאמר: באשה אינו ולד, אלמא אינו מתקיים, והא חשיב ליה גבי מומי כהן, אלמא חי; אבל לשמואל, דאמר: באשה ולד, מתקיים, לא פריך מידי. ובבהמה נמי, אר"ת דמתקיים לשמואל; והא דאמר בסמוך דכי יצא לאויר העולם אסור, היינו משום שסועה דאסר רחמנא. ורש"י פירש בסמוך לפי שיטתו, דאסור משום נפל; ושסועה דאסר רחמנא, היינו מין בהמה דעלמא שיש לאם ולולד שני גבין וכן ב' שדראות, אבל הנולד מבהמה שאין לה אלא גב אחד ושדרה אחת לא איצטריך קרא למיסר, דנפל גמור הוי. ובאשה מיהא מתקיים אף לפירושו, מדקאמר באשה ולד; וללישנא דבעלמא אגמריה, משמע כפירושו. וא"ת: בפרק אלו טרפות (חולין ס:) דפריך גבי שסועה שיש לה ב' גבין, וכי משה קניגי היה? והשתא לפ"ה אתי שפיר, דשסועה מין בעלמא הוא לשמואל, ואינה מצויה אלא ביער, לכך קאמר וכי קניגי היה; אבל לפי' ר"ת, שאף לשמואל אינו מין בפני עצמו, אלא שכך נולד מן הבהמה, מה ענין זה אצל קניגי? וי"ל, דאף לפירוש ר"ת, אם לא היה קניגי ורגיל לראות ומכיר בהמות משונות, לא היה מכיר בהמה זו שיש לה ב' גבין, אע"פ שגם נולד מבהמות של ישוב, שאינה רגילה להוליד מבהמה שאינה משונה:
Tosafot on Niddah 24a:15:1.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: Any [creature] that has, etc. - Rashi explained: Since it is a blemish for a sacrifice, by implication it is permitted for ordinary [consumption]. And it is difficult for both of them [Rav and Shmuel], for behold, [according to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus] it is permitted even if it emerged into the airspace of the world, whereas Shmuel permitted it only in its mother's womb. And it is difficult according to Rabbeinu Tam, for in the chapter "Elu Mumin" (Bekhorot 43b) it was taught among the blemishes of a priest, and not among the blemishes of an animal! And there too, [the Gemara] raises an objection against Rav, and does not cite anything from Shmuel. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that [the Gemara] specifically objected against Rav, who said: "In [the case of] a woman, it is not an offspring" — evidently it cannot survive; yet behold, it reckons him among the blemishes of a priest, evidently he lives! But against Shmuel, who said that in [the case of] a woman it is an offspring, [which implies that] it survives, it does not object at all. And in [the case of] an animal as well, Rabbeinu Tam says that it can survive according to Shmuel; and that which [the Gemara] states nearby, that once it has emerged into the airspace of the world it is forbidden, that is on account of [the prohibition of] the cloven creature (shesu'ah), which the Merciful One forbade. And Rashi explained nearby according to his own approach, that it is forbidden because it is a non-viable birth (nefel); and [as for] the cloven creature that the Merciful One forbade, that is an independent species of animal in the world in which [both] mother and offspring have two backs and likewise two spines. But one born from an animal that has only one back and one spine did not require a verse to forbid it, for it is an absolute non-viable birth. And in [the case of] a woman, at any rate, it can survive even according to his [Rashi's] explanation, since [Shmuel] says: "In [the case of] a woman, it is an offspring." And according to the formulation, "He taught it to him in the world," it supports his [Rashi's] explanation. And if you should say: In the chapter "Elu Tereifot" (Chullin 60b), where [the Gemara] objects regarding the cloven creature that has two backs: "Was Moses a hunter?" — now, according to the explanation of Rashi, it works out well, since the cloven creature is an independent species in the world according to Shmuel, and it is found only in the forest; that is why it says, "Was he a hunter?" But according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, that even according to Shmuel it is not a distinct species in its own right, but rather it is simply born like this from an animal, what does this have to do with a hunter? And one can say that even according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, if he were not a hunter and accustomed to seeing and being familiar with abnormal animals, he would not have known of this animal that has two backs, even though it is also born from domesticated animals of human settlements, as an animal that is not abnormal does not commonly give birth [to such an abnormality].

Tosafot on Niddah 24a:1:1.hebrew: עד הארכובה - והארכובה בכלל, דהיינו מן הארכובה ולמעלה. ואין שייך להביא זה גבי כל שיעורי חכמים להחמיר לענין עד ועד בכלל באלו טרפות (חולין נה.). ואע"ג דתבנית יד אמרי' בפרקין דטמאה לידה, היינו כשניכר שהמותר נמחה כשפירש; א"נ, כאן מיירי דניכר היטב שלא נברא יותר, כגון במקום החסרון יש עור נקרם:
Tosafot on Niddah 24a:1:1.english: Until the knee - And the knee [joint] is included, that is, from the knee and above. And it is not relevant to cite this regarding [the principle that] "all measures of the Sages are to be stringent" with respect to [whether] "until" [means] "until and including" in [the chapter of] "Elu Terefot" (Chullin 55a). And even though we say in our chapter that [one who discharges] the form of a hand is impure with [the impurity of] childbirth, that is when it is discernible that the remainder [of the fetus] dissolved when it separated. Alternatively, here [our Gemara] is dealing with [a case where] it is clearly discernible that nothing more was ever formed, such as where at the place of the deficiency skin had formed over.

Tosafot on Niddah 24a:7:1.hebrew: ליתני שמא מגוף אטום באת או ממי שפניו כו' - וא"ת: והא איכא טובא דלא תני, כגון פניו תייש, (ופניו) אטום, ואפקותא דדיקלא? וי"ל, דפניו מוסמסין דומה לגוף אטום, והויא ליה למיתני בהדיה טפי מאחריני:
Tosafot on Niddah 24a:7:1.english: Let it teach: Perhaps it came from a sealed body or from one whose face, etc. - And if you say: But behold, there are many [cases] that [the baraita] does not teach, such as [a fetus whose] face is [like that of] a goat, (and its face is) sealed, and [a fetus shaped like] an offshoot of a palm tree (afkuta dedikla)? And one can say: That [a fetus whose] face is mashed is similar to a sealed body, and [the baraita] should have taught [it] together with it more than the others.

Tosafot on Niddah 24a:8:1.hebrew: אמר רב פפא בפניו מוסמסין כ"ע לא פליגי - והא דקאמר איתיביה ר' יוחנן לר"ל, לא היו דברים מעולם. וכענין זה יש בריש חולין (דף ד):
Tosafot on Niddah 24a:8:1.english: Rav Pappa says: In [a case where] its face is mashed, everyone agrees - And that which [the Gemara] says, "Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish" — these things never happened. And there is a similar case at the beginning of Chullin (daf 4).
